minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission voted to allow one large headstone over four or six South Cemetery plots; mowing dispute stayed unresolved.
minutes.summary: The commission, with no DPW director or superintendent present at the start, spent most of the meeting on the continuing failure to get the cemeteries mowed to standard, hearing a resident veteran's complaint and later the town's Heather. It also covered a missing Allen headstone trust, a robotic mower idea, Rainmaker record-keeping, flag illumination and capital funding. Two formal votes were taken: approving the May 16 minutes and permitting the headstone; the meeting then adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Frustration with the cemetery mowing and upkeep around Memorial Day, absence of town and DPW officials, broken headstones, clutter by the cemetery building; offered to help and to bring veterans' organizations.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the May 16th meeting (with a typo correction of plane to plan).
Allow a single 4 by 1 headstone in South Cemetery centered over either four or six family plots.

budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director's written report gave a total of man hours for mowing around Memorial Day without stating the time period; members questioned whether the hours were plausible.
Only a small balance reportedly remains in the trust that pays for periodic cleaning of a headstone; no trust document has been found.
A member described robotic mower models and their price range as something to explore, possibly with grant money.
The vendor gave a rough informal estimate for a full migration of the cemetery records, with no quote based on actual volume.

budget_items.topic: Headstone washing and repair of oldest section
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the DPW director's cost figure differs from the figure submitted to capital planning for repairing 1700-1800s headstones.
Lot sale revenue arrives in July; the chair listed expected funds for FY2025 and upcoming costs such as a Rainmaker license, and noted further money requires a fall town meeting vote.
The DPW has no funding for the project to improve grass and treat grubs, so it would need the capital plan.
Heather said capital requests for fiscal 25 far exceeded available funding and are prioritized by criteria; a member said the cemetery's share is too small to fix mowing.
The chair bought inexpensive solar lights as a trial; the DPW director is getting a quote from a contractor to run electricity to flag poles.

decisions.decision: Heather agreed to follow up on the robot mower idea, including contacting a local grant source and considering a trial elsewhere in town.
Heather agreed to follow up with the DPW director to get a quote for electricity to illuminate the flags.
The chair will try to get a quote from Rainmaker, via the DPW director, on the cost of the records migration.
The Allen headstone trust search continues; the chair will speak with the finance director after the meeting.
Heather was asked to look into how the DPW and contractor mowing hour figures were derived and report back.

what_happened.line: The Cemetery Commission voted to allow one large headstone centered over either four or six family plots in South Cemetery.
Most of the meeting went to the continuing failure to get the cemeteries mowed to standard, with no resolution reached.
A resident veteran told the commission that upkeep around Memorial Day fell short and offered to bring veterans' organizations to help.
The commission was asked to look into how the DPW and contractor mowing hour figures were derived, with a report back to follow.
Follow-ups were assigned on a robotic mower idea, a records-migration quote from Rainmaker, flag lighting, and the missing Allen headstone trust.

why_it_matters: Cemetery mowing and headstone repair compete with every other town request for capital money, and the commission said its share is too small to fix mowing, so conditions at the cemeteries may not change until that funding question is settled.
Families buying South Cemetery plots now have a vote allowing one large headstone over four or six plots, which affects what a plot holder may place.
watch_next: Heather's report on how the DPW and contractor mowing hour figures were derived.
Quotes for the Rainmaker records migration and for electricity to light the flags, plus any fall town meeting vote on further cemetery money.
